rationale: Lycopolitan plural variant of ⲙⲟⲩⲉⲩⲉ 'waters' (already in glossary). The ⲗ-form should be added as a recognized orthographic variant. Distinct in this kephalaion from the homograph ⲙⲟⲩⲗⲉⲩⲉ 'counsels' (Greek βουλεύω). Disambiguated by hydrological-cosmological context (falls from heaven, paired with fire/darkness as elements).
Lycopolitan reflex of ϩⲉ 'fall.' Used cosmologically here of waters falling from heaven. The ⲍⲉⲗⲉ form (with ⲍ for ϩ and intrusive vowel) is dialectal.

Standard Manichaean cosmological figure (rex gloriae) — distinct from the King of Honor (ⲡⲣ̄ⲣⲟ ⲙⲡⲧⲁⲓⲟ in vocab). Here he is the operator of the three cosmic wheels (fire/water/wind) summoned by a sign from the Living Spirit. Greek βασιλεὺς τῆς δόξης.

Chapter title (kephalaion 41). ⲗⲁⲥ 'tongue' + ⲫⲁⲗⲁⲥⲥⲁ 'sea.' Possibly refers to the linguistic/discursive correspondence of the cosmic seas — the speech that the encircling waters utter, paired with the 'Error and Answering' (ⲡⲥⲁⲣⲙⲉ ⲙⲛ ⲡⲟⲩⲱⲍⲙⲉ) of the three deceitful places mentioned in the kephalaion's opening.

proposed_english: the Omophoros that bears the lands
rationale: ϫⲱⲃⲥ̄ here functions as 'bear/support' rather than 'cover.' Technical Manichaean cosmological epithet of the cosmic Atlas (Pillar of Glory) who supports the earths from below — the conduit through which the three powers (wind/water/fire) ascend.

Compound spatial term ⲥⲁ-ⲛ-ⲃⲁⲗ 'side of outside' = 'the outside, exterior region.' Pair-partner with ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ ('the upper side') and ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ ('the lower side'). Recurs throughout this kephalaion as the destination of expelled darkness/fire.
